continuity_scope: The Princess Bride, 1987 feature-film adaptation continuity only. This pass uses the American Film Institute Catalog's film synopsis and the Criterion Collection's licensed film-edition description and cast/credits. It excludes William Goldman's novel as an independent witness, stage versions, games, and later derivative works.
coverage_rule: Include central named individual dramatic characters directly named and described in the selected AFI synopsis and/or Criterion film description: Buttercup, Westley, Prince Humperdinck, Vizzini, Fezzik, Inigo Montoya, and Count Rugen. The Dread Pirate Roberts is recorded only as Westley's explicit role alias, not a second person. Frame readers whose only individual designation is a role label, unnamed guards, the father of Inigo, and generic soldiers/occupations remain outside this narrow pass.
omissions: The Grandfather and Grandson frame characters, whose selected sources supply role labels but no personal names or claim-specific comparison records in this narrow pass.
Inigo's unnamed father, unnamed guards, soldiers, bishop/clergyman, Albino, king, queen, and all generic groups.
The Dread Pirate Roberts as a separate character node; AFI states the role is passed down and Westley takes it.
Fictional places, poisons, artifacts, occupations, frame-story structures, and motifs as character nodes.
William Goldman's novel, stage versions, games, and later derivative works.
content_cautions: AFI's film synopsis includes kidnapping, forced betrothal, planned murder, fencing/combat, a torture device, threats, attempted self-harm, and deaths. This pass records only narrow relationship/premise claims and does not reproduce scenes or provide detailed violence descriptions.

Fezzik is called a giant in the film materials and Count Rugen is described as six-fingered. These are fictional screen descriptors, not real-world disability, anatomy, diagnosis, height, or social-identity classifications.

Criterion characterizes the film as an irreverent fairy-tale classic with gags and spoofery. Neither parody nor fairy-tale framing is used to deny the narrative's in-film coercion/threat content or to convert it into a literal real-world model.
uncertainties: The selected references are official film summary/edition material rather than a full authorized screenplay with page citations; all claims remain at the synopsis/official-reference level.
No claim is made about novel-only, stage-only, or derivative continuity identities, powers, outcomes, or relationships.

The selected sources establish Westley's Dread Pirate Roberts role explicitly but do not warrant merging every masked/pirate appellation or using role names as separate people beyond the stated alias.

The selected sources do not give sufficient evidence to map fictional poisons, torture effects, giant terminology, six-fingered anatomy, or true-love language onto real-world medical, disability, legal, or ethical categories.
evidence_basis: AFI's official Catalog synopsis provides the 1987-film plot and character-action evidence. Criterion's licensed film edition supplies 1987 film identity, cast-role confirmations, and its fairy-tale/spoofery framing. No fan wiki or Wikipedia was used.

supports: 1987-film plot events, named-character roles, explicit Westley/Dread Pirate Roberts identity, Buttercup/Westley relationship, kidnapping, Humperdinck, Vizzini, Fezzik, Inigo, and Rugen claims.
